articles.title: Your first game starts here.
articles.intro: Choose a package, prepare the TV and keep your settings when updating.

sections.title: A quick equipment check
text: You need a Samsung TV with Tizen 5.5 or later, a compatible controller and a PC running VibeShine or Sunshine. Use the same local network for initial setup.
sections.callout: Start with 1080p · 60 FPS · H.264 · 30 Mbps. Adjust to your TV and connection.

sections.title: Normal or ForceGM?
text: The packages share the same code and app identity. The in-app ultra-low latency switch is a separate setting.

cards.title: Normal
cards.text: Does not request panel Game Mode. A starting point if you are unsure.

cards.title: ForceGM
cards.text: Requests panel Game Mode. Its effect depends on the TV and system version.

sections.title: Install on your Samsung TV
steps: Download a VibeLight .wgt from Releases and Apps2Samsung from its official project.
In TV Apps / App Settings, enter 12345, enable Developer Mode, enter the installer device’s IP and restart the TV. Menus vary by model.
Open Apps2Samsung, choose the TV and select your .wgt. Follow its signing and installation prompts.

illustration.caption: Setup diagram, not a Samsung or Apps2Samsung screenshot. Follow the controls shown by your version.

sections.title: Update without starting over
text: Reuse your signing profile and author certificate. Avoid uninstalling the app or regenerating your certificate. Review any installer prompt that proposes removing the existing app.
sections.callout: Uninstalling can erase pairing, preferences and local records. Normal and ForceGM update the same installation when the signature is compatible.

sections.title: Prefer Tizen Studio?
text: Install TV Extensions and Samsung Certificate Extension. Connect the TV in Device Manager and allow app installation. Import the WGT, use a Samsung profile covering the TV’s DUID, then repackage/sign and run it. Reuse the existing author certificate for updates.

articles.title: Let the TV find your PC.
articles.intro: Set up the host once. Pairing links your TV to the right computer.

sections.title: Prepare VibeShine or Sunshine
text: Install and open the host on your PC. Follow its setup for capture, encoder and permissions. Add games under Applications; Desktop is a simple first connection.

sections.title: Confirm the PIN
steps: Open VibeLight and select the PC. If it is missing, use Add PC and enter the computer’s local IP.
Enter the PIN shown on the TV into the PIN page of the host’s web interface.
Wait for pairing to finish, then open your game library.

image.name: pair
image.caption: Pairing screen with a demonstration PIN. Never share your real PIN or network details.
image.alt: Pairing screen with a demonstration PIN. Never share your real PIN or network details.

annotations: Read the PIN on the TV.
Enter it on the PC, in the host’s PIN page — not in the installer.

sections.title: Wake the PC
text: Wake PC uses Wake-on-LAN. Enable it in BIOS/UEFI and the network adapter, and verify the physical adapter’s MAC in that PC’s settings. Wi-Fi and waking after shutdown depend on the hardware. This does not add a power-off action.

articles.title: Everything within reach.
articles.intro: Start a game, return to it and choose exactly how to leave.

sections.title: Play or resume
text: Connect the controller to the TV, choose a game and select Play. Resume reconnects to the running app. The connection view shows its current stage; Cancel stops the attempt.

sections.title: Open the in-game menu
text: Press Guide/Home on the gamepad. From this menu you can return to the game, adjust volume, show statistics, disconnect or close the game on the PC.

image.name: menu
image.caption: The real menu rendered locally over an open-source game illustration.
image.alt: The real menu rendered locally over an open-source game illustration.

annotations: Resume closes this menu and returns to the game.
Statistics starts a local record for this session.
Disconnect keeps the game on the PC; End game on PC requests closure and asks for confirmation.
sections.callout: Closing the game may lose unsaved progress. Leaving through Smart Hub disconnects locally; reopen VibeLight and Resume to reconnect.

sections.title: New game missing?
text: Refresh library asks the PC for the game list again. It does not restart VibeLight. To reopen the whole app, use General & about → Restart app.

articles.title: Tune what matters.
articles.intro: Six categories, with the effect of each adjustment close at hand.

sections.title: Find the right category
text: Picture: resolution, FPS, bitrate, codec, HDR, color range, frame pacing and ultra-low latency. Sound: channels, adaptive buffer ceiling and playback on the PC.

Controls: mapping, tests, sticks, triggers, rumble and mouse. PCs & library: address input, host resolution, ordering and PC removal. Diagnosis: warnings and saved records. General & about: language, menu sounds, help, restart and restore defaults.

image.name: picture
image.caption: Picture settings in the current source. Values are illustrative.
image.alt: Picture settings in the current source. Values are illustrative.

sections.title: Ultra-low latency and ForceGM
text: Ultra-low video latency selects a player mode that disables TV image enhancements to reduce delay. It is independent of ForceGM and remains off by default. Some TVs/system versions may be unstable; Tizen 9 has a history of black screens or freezing.
Frame pacing can improve motion regularity and add latency. Keep the setting that works for your TV.
sections.keywords: lag latency game mode forcegm pacing h264

sections.title: Why not choose the smallest audio buffer?
text: The setting is an adaptive ceiling, not a fixed delay. Audio normally starts around 20 ms and increases its margin after underruns. A smaller ceiling can cause gaps or crackling without improving a session that is already stable.
sections.callout: Change one setting at a time. Compare similar scenes and recording durations.

sections.title: Make the controller yours
text: Use Controls to map buttons, test inputs and adjust sticks or triggers. The direct tuning shortcut opens the existing editor. Menu sounds live in General & about; they stop before streaming.

articles.title: Good questions. Useful numbers.
articles.intro: Record deliberately, review locally and compare sessions with context.

sections.title: Start only when you choose
steps: During a game, open the gamepad menu and enable Statistics. Recording starts then.
Hide the numbers whenever you like. The same session keeps recording until you leave.
After leaving, open Settings → Diagnosis → Last diagnosis.
sections.callout: Statistics stay on this TV. Nothing is sent. A new session starts inactive; without activation in that game, nothing is recorded.

sections.title: Your last ten session records
text: History & comparison keeps the latest ten saved sessions. Saving the eleventh removes the oldest. A session without activation does not replace previous records. Late activation is marked as partial coverage.

image.name: history
image.caption: Ten artificial session records. A and B mark the selected pair.
image.alt: Ten artificial session records. A and B mark the selected pair.

annotations: Select any two distinct records with OK; select again to deselect.
A third record never replaces a selection silently. Deselect one first.

sections.title: Compare A and B
text: Choose Compare 2 records. The columns show each session and the difference B − A, with units and the values of settings that differ. Back preserves your selection and returns to the previous row.

image.name: comparison
image.caption: Side-by-side comparison. Numbers are illustrative, not TV test results.
image.alt: Side-by-side comparison. Numbers are illustrative, not TV test results.

annotations: Check configuration, scene and recording duration before comparing.
Event rates use the time actually measured; counts and denominators remain visible.
There is no automatic winner. Missing data is unavailable, never a healthy zero.

sections.title: Nine groups, with room for detail
text: Transmission, FPS, smoothness, network, frames, PC processing, TV work, audio and events. Live FPS/native values use the latest window; percentiles, peaks and counters cover the recorded interval. Saved means cover the recording.

Technical details preserves clock, cadence, window deviation, frame load, TV CPU/memory, JavaScript delays and worst-episode context. Native measurement coverage is explicit. p95 means 95% of measurements were at or below that value.

RTT is network round-trip time. Clock and submission to the player do not measure button-to-image latency. Browser presentation is not a physical panel measurement. A mean of window percentiles is not a session percentile.

articles.title: Find your way back to the game.
articles.intro: Start with the symptom. Try one change and check the result.

sections.title: PC missing or PIN rejected
text: Check that the host is open, both devices share a network and the firewall allows the host. Add the PC by local IP, then enter the new PIN in that host’s web interface. A failed response does not prove the PC is powered off.

sections.title: Black screen, freezing or uneven motion
text: Check the TV’s supported resolution and codec. Keep ultra-low latency off, especially on Tizen 9. If VibeLight reports failed cleanup and asks for a restart, restart before reconnecting.
For stutters despite high average FPS, enable Statistics and inspect interval p95/max, frame gaps and RTT variation. Compare equivalent scenes.
sections.keywords: stutter hitch fps black screen frozen

sections.title: Audio gaps or crackling
text: Check the output device and adaptive buffer ceiling. A low ceiling leaves less room for variation. In the diagnosis, inspect underruns/overruns and actual/target buffer.

sections.title: No saved record, or a storage error?
text: Enable Statistics in the game menu, leave the session and look in Settings → Diagnosis. Sessions never activated do not create records.
If saving fails, previous history is preserved and the new session may not be saved. Do not uninstall to recover records.

articles.title: Independent. Open source.
articles.intro: VibeLight is a Moonlight Tizen fork for streaming PC games to Samsung TVs.

sections.title: Project and support
text: Use the project’s issues for reproducible problems. Include app version, TV/Tizen and steps. Hide private network data and credentials in screenshots.

sections.title: Which version does this guide describe?
text: Reviewed {{reviewed}}. This guide describes current source, including the upcoming settings and session history. The available release is {{published}}; these screens and the ten-session history are not in its packages.
Check your installed release notes before expecting a feature. The source revision is shown in the footer; no next release number is promised.

sections.title: Images, licenses and technical references
text: App screens use artificial PCs, games and measurements. Installation artwork is a diagram. They do not claim physical TV validation or endorsement by Samsung or game developers. Open-game artwork retains its original credits and licenses.
